request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the ROLLUP and TOTALS audit lines, and all 4 acceptance tests now pass in `bin/e2e`.

**One difference from the request:** the request says `ROLLUP name=<name>`, but the test expects `person=<name>` (for example `ROLLUP sheet=… by=uma person=Ada claimed=0.00 due-total=0.00`). I followed the test.

**How it works:**
- **New service:** `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/Rollup.java` works out each person's claimed and due-total on the server, plus the sheet's two totals. These figures were previously only calculated in the browser, so it uses the same rules: a settled or stated claim keeps its fixed figure, and a due-total shows `n/a` when no rate applies.
- **Before and after:** every change takes a snapshot of the figures before it writes anything. After its own audit line, it writes one ROLLUP line for each person whose figures moved, in the order people were added; a newly added person always counts as moved. If either sheet total moved, a TOTALS line follows. A change that moves nothing adds no lines.
- **Where it's hooked in:** adding or editing a person, adding or editing a claim, opening, settling or voiding a claim, setting a rate, taking a statement, and changing the sheet's today. Changing today still writes no line of its own.
- **Refused changes:** these fail before the after-check, so they add no rollup lines.

No database or front-end changes were needed.
